notes: Five documents (Provost syllabus language, Provost generative AI page, ai.asu.edu resources, CLAS AI resources, AI MS handbook); units aligned by source passage, 65 matched. Main disagreements on matched units: (1) unit_stance on citation/disclosure duties (A require, B permit; set to permit because they are conditions on permitted use) and on integrity-violation sentences (set by what the sentence says about use: restrict/prohibit when it classes use as a violation, neutral for consequences of nondisclosure); (2) actor and phase for informational sentences (student vs all; general vs during-work or over-time; set by the audience of the section and by whether any course moment is named); (3) policy type for approved-tool sentences (P92 list vs P65 approval process, split across the two sentences), Career Services (P44 vs P87, set to P87), CLAS delegation (P04 vs P85, kept P04 with a fit note), 'document expectations' vs 'open dialogs' (A merged, split into P09 and P66), and group-member AI use (P71 vs UNCOVERED, kept UNCOVERED); (4) modality for 'not sufficient evidence to begin an investigation' (informs vs must-not, set to should-not because the text goes on 'we recommend') and for the no-AI tier (must vs must-not, set to must-not); (5) policy null vs normalized: A's normalized wording added 'set' or joined two rules in three units, so those were set to null or the second rule split out. Document stance: Provost generative AI page was delegates for A and encourage for B; set to encourage because it welcomes AI and recommends platforms without handing the decision to instructors. Unmatched: A found 6 that B missed (5 kept, 1 dropped as a repeat of the P84 process unit); B found 9 that A missed (7 kept, 2 dropped: a feature description of efficacy-research data and a pointer to webinar recordings). No new types; one UNCOVERED unit (group-member AI use) kept for the theme review.
